messages.content: Write a customer case study about a company that adopted a continuous delivery platform and now deploys more often. Around 250 words.

**Meridian Freight Systems: from Thursday nights to Tuesday afternoons**

Meridian Freight builds routing software for regional trucking companies. Until 2024 it shipped once every three weeks, on a Thursday night, with four engineers on a call and a rollback plan nobody had rehearsed.

"The release wasn't the scary part," says Dana Okonkwo, who runs platform engineering. "The scary part was batching six weeks of work and having no idea which piece broke things."

Meridian moved to a continuous delivery platform in March 2024. The migration took eleven weeks, not the two the vendor's estimate suggested. Most of the overrun was Meridian's own doing: the test suite had gone flaky years earlier, and nobody noticed because releases were rare enough to babysit by hand. Five of the eleven weeks went to fixing tests before anything touched a pipeline.

The numbers after twelve months: roughly 40 deploys a week, against 17 in the whole of 2023. Median time from merge to production is 22 minutes. Change failure rate sits at 3.1%; there is no honest before-number, because Meridian wasn't tracking it.

Some things did not move. The on-call rotation is the same size. Support ticket volume is flat. Okonkwo is direct about that: "We ship more often. No customer asked us to. What they actually got is that a bug reported Monday morning is fixed Monday afternoon, instead of waiting for the next window."

Meridian runs a single Go monolith with one database. Teams carrying more services, or a compliance sign-off between merge and release, should expect a different curve.

---
